episode.title: Why Won't These DICE Change Their Number?

synopsis: A man repeatedly rolls a pair of ordinary dice, but they inexplicably always land on the exact same number, defying probability.
narration: Playing a board game, my dice kept landing on the same number. I thought it was a fluke, but it's been happening for ages. It's so weird.

shots.prompt: A pair of standard white plastic dice, each with crisp black pips marking their faces, slightly rounded edges from use, and a familiar lightweight feel. The dice possess an inherent, unwavering property that forces them to always land with specific, predefined faces pointing upwards, regardless of the force or angle of the roll, defying probabilistic outcomes. A close-up view of the two dice on a dark wood coffee table, with hands entering the frame to roll them. A familiar living-room coffee table: dark wood top with two pale water rings, a folded magazine at the frame edge, the soft blur of a sofa behind, and warm lamp light mixed with grey window daylight. A pair of hands wearing a plain black crew-neck t-shirt shake and roll two white plastic dice onto a dark wood coffee table, and after tumbling, both dice visibly land on their faces, each displaying exactly two black pips on their upward-facing surface. The view stays in one unchanging position and angle for the whole shot.
shots.violation_observation: After being rolled, both dice visibly land on their faces, each displaying exactly two black pips on their upward-facing surface.
